AU-01 Unified staff sign-in

MVP1-CORE
G1 IDENTITY & ACCESS — AUTH ENTRY
Baseline: EXTENDS · AU-S7…S13 entry doors → one templated sign-in
Purpose & workflow: Single sign-in entry for all staff roles across a tenant's Keycloak staff realm. The workspace-realm context chip makes the tenant explicit before credentials are typed; white-label branding is applied per tenant. On success the user proceeds to two-factor verification (AU-03) or to enrolment (AU-04) if their role mandates a factor they have not registered.

AU-02 Sign-in failures & throttling

MVP1-CORE
G1 IDENTITY & ACCESS — AUTH ENTRY
Baseline: EXTENDS · AU-S1/S4 failure & lockout states
Purpose & workflow: Defines every failure path off AU-01: wrong password with attempts-remaining counter, progressive throttling with a visible countdown, hard lock after the policy threshold, and a distinct suspended-account message. Copy is written to avoid account enumeration — failure text never confirms whether an email exists, and suspension is only disclosed after a correct password.

AU-04 Two-factor enrolment

MVP1-CORE
G1 IDENTITY & ACCESS — AUTH ENTRY
Baseline: EXTENDS · AU-S2 enrolment + backup codes
Purpose & workflow: Forced interstitial after first sign-in (or when an admin resets factors). The user chooses passkey (recommended), TOTP, or both; must verify a first code before the factor is saved; then receives 10 single-use backup codes shown exactly once. Enrolment is mandatory before workspace entry for privileged roles (org admin, radiologist sign-off, cashier refunds) per policy AUTH-POL-05.

AU-05 Lost authenticator recovery

MVP1-CORE
G1 IDENTITY & ACCESS — AUTH ENTRY
Baseline: NET-NEW · P2 lost-authenticator recovery
Purpose & workflow: High-assurance path when a user has lost every second factor (authenticator and backup codes). Identity is re-proven in layers: correct password, then a manager/org-admin approval task (four-eyes), plus an optional cooling period per tenant policy. Access stays denied throughout; on approval all sessions are revoked and the user must re-enrol factors (AU-04) before re-entering the workspace.

AU-06 Password reset & policy

MVP1-CORE
G1 Identity & Access — auth entry + session
Baseline: EXTENDS · AU-S5 reset + policy
Purpose & workflow: Staff who forget their password request a reset from the sign-in page. The system always shows the same neutral confirmation (no account enumeration), then delivers a one-time link by email plus a 6-digit OTP that must be entered together. The new password must satisfy org policy (min 12 chars, last-5 history block, no forced periodic rotation); on success all other sessions are revoked.

AU-08 Session lock & shared terminal

MVP1-CORE
G1 Identity & Access — auth entry + session
Baseline: NET-NEW · P2 session lock & shared-terminal switch
Purpose & workflow: Personal workstations auto-lock after inactivity and resume with the user's PIN or password. Shared counter terminals (front office, cashier) use badge-tap or PIN fast user switching with a target of under 3 seconds, so queues keep moving without shared logins. A "whose session" banner is always visible so actions are attributed to the right person.

Implementation noteStep-up issues a short-lived confirmation token bound to the session AND the specific target object (e.g. the report being signed) — prevents CSRF/replay.
Audit line format structured, append-only
stepup.<pass|fail|expired> · actor=<user> · action=<verb.object> · target=<id> · mech=<passkey|totp|password> · attempt=n/N · <ts IST> · term=<terminal>
Confirmations are single-use and bound to the exact action payload shown in the modal — a confirmation cannot be replayed for a different target. Expired confirmations (5 min) require a fresh step-up.

Viewing the matrix is logged read-only; any edit to a matrix row requires step-up (passkey) plus counter-approval by a second admin, both recorded in the access log.

STATE C — DELETION REQUEST: WHAT WE CAN AND CANNOT DELETE YET
◎ Magnus Diagnostics · North Paravoor
Before you ask us to delete PLEASE READ

We take deletion seriously and will remove everything we are allowed to. But some records must be kept for a fixed time under Indian law, even after you ask. In plain words:

WhatKept untilWhy (the law)
Scan reports & medical records3 years after your last visitMedical-records retention rules for diagnostic centres
Invoices & payment receipts8 years from the financial yearGST & income-tax record-keeping rules
Consent forms you signedAs long as the record they coverProof that we had your permission
X-ray / CT dose recordsPer AERB rulesRadiation-safety regulations

What we CAN do now: stop all reminders and marketing, remove your data from any research or analytics use, delete contact details not tied to a legal record, and lock the rest so it is only touched if the law demands it. When each retention period ends, the records are deleted automatically — you don't need to ask again.

Purpose & workflow: The Help link in the footer of every patient page lands here. It answers the four most common problems (no OTP, wrong/old mobile number, expired link, stuck payment) with plain checklists, gives the clinic's phone number and hours, and lets the patient report a problem — which creates a tracked grievance (GRV) reference. ◎ Magnus Diagnostics · North Paravoor
⚠ This page is not for medical emergencies. If someone is seriously unwell, call 108 (ambulance) or go to the nearest hospital emergency department now.
Common problems — tap to open
I didn't get the OTP code ▴
✓
Wait 60 seconds — SMS can be slow at busy times. Then tap Resend code (allowed 3 times).
✓
Check the phone with the number ending in the digits shown on screen — the OTP goes to your registered mobile, which may not be the phone in your hand.
✓
If you use SMS-blocking / DND apps, check the blocked folder for sender MRDIAG.
✓
Still nothing after 3 tries? Call the clinic below — we can verify you by phone and re-send.
My registered mobile number is wrong or old ▾
For your safety we cannot change your number over the internet. Visit any Magnus branch with a photo ID (any one of passport, driving licence, voter ID, or Aadhaar — we record only the last 4 digits). The front office updates it in minutes and OTPs work immediately after.
The link says it has expired ▾
Report and reminder links stop working after a set time to protect you. Ask for a fresh link by calling the clinic, or collect a printed copy at the branch with photo ID. Expired links can never be revived — a new one is always issued instead.
My payment is stuck / money left my account ▾
If UPI money was debited but the page didn't confirm: don't pay again. Failed UPI payments auto-return within 2–5 working days by NPCI rules. Note your UPI/UTR reference from your bank app and call us — receipt RCP/NPV/26-27/0xxx is issued the moment the money is confirmed on our side.

FO-01 Reception dashboard & token board

MVP1-CORE
G3 Front Office & Reception — workspace 'Front Office'
Baseline: EXTENDS · FO-S1 Reception dashboard
Purpose & workflow: The front-office executive (D. Nair) keeps this board open all day to watch the live token queue, appointment arrivals and per-modality load, and to call the next patient to a service point. FO-02 Patient search

MVP1-CORE
G3 Front Office & Reception — workspace 'Front Office'
Baseline: EXTENDS · FO-S2 Patient search
Purpose & workflow: Front-office staff search before every booking or registration so duplicates are never created. Exact identifiers (MRN, phone, ABHA, insurance ID) return authoritative hits; name + DOB runs a fuzzy match with confidence chips. The screen must guarantee that every search is recorded with a purpose, results are masked to the minimum needed to disambiguate, and a failed search never shows a partial list that could be mistaken for "no match".

FO-04 Registration — duplicate review step

G3 Front Office & Reception — workspace 'Front Office'

FO-05 Registration — consent capture

MVP1-CORE
G3 Front Office & Reception — workspace 'Front Office'
Baseline: EXTENDS · FO-S3 Registration — consent step
Purpose & workflow: Final registration step: the patient (or guardian for minors) reviews the clinic privacy notice in their preferred language and grants purpose-level consent. Care and billing purposes are required to receive services; notifications and analytics are optional — analytics is unavailable for children. If a patient declines a required purpose, registration is not blocked: the refusal is recorded and flagged to the privacy team for follow-up. Staff-assisted (read-aloud) consent requires an attestation.

Lane rules
✓Separate lanes for walk-in vs booked — booked patients hold their slot time; walk-ins queue FIFO in their own lane. Interleave ratio:

STATE C — POLICY CARD (WHO MAY STAT · AUTO-DOWNGRADE RULE)
Orders › STAT & priority governance › Policy
Priority policy — chain level v3 · effective 01-Jun-2026
Maintained by chain medical board; branch admins cannot edit. Displayed read-only at every order-entry point.
Who may mark STAT
ActorMay mark STAT?Conditions
Internal radiologistYesJustification text mandatory (free text ≥ 15 chars)
Verified external referrerYesJustification mandatory; subject to monthly governance thresholds (≤12% rate, ≥60% true-urgency)
Front office (D. Nair et al.)Only on physician instructionMust capture instructing physician's name + callback number in the order
Unverified / pending referrer (OR-08)NoPriority capped at Urgent until directory verification completes
Patient self-requestNoNever — convenience is not urgency
Auto-downgrade rule radiologist confirm always required
1 · Detect
System flags a STAT order when justification is blank, matches an administrative-reason lexicon, or the orderer is under a governance restriction.
2 · Radiologist confirm
The flagged order is queued to the duty radiologist with the justification text and clinical context. No priority is ever lowered automatically. The radiologist either confirms STAT or downgrades to Urgent/Routine with a reason code, signed under their own identity.
3 · Notify
Orderer is notified of the downgrade with the reason; the event feeds the monthly governance report. Downgrade never delays an already-checked-in patient's safety screening.
Priority ladder & SLAs
STAT
Acquire ≤ 60 min · report ≤ 2h · OVERDUE 00:42 example: ACC-2026-91366, owner Dr. A. Rao · Escalated to Dr. V. Shetty
Urgent
Acquire same day · report ≤ 6h · due in 3h
Routine
Report ≤ 24h · due in 18h
Why governance mattersWhen 1 in 5 orders is STAT, none are. Thresholds are reviewed quarterly by the medical board.
Policy version history
01-Jun-26v3 — added referrer restriction mechanism (30-day radiologist confirm)
10-Feb-26v2 — administrative-reason lexicon introduced
01-Nov-25v1 — initial policy, thresholds 12% / 60%

Every STAT flag, review verdict, privilege restriction and priority downgrade is signed with the acting clinician's identity and reason code; report views with masked patient identifiers, and any unmasking (which requires a declared clinical purpose), are recorded in the access log.

CS-04 Physician override — blocked screening

MVP1-CORE
G5 Clinical Safety
Baseline: NET-NEW · closes S-2 physician-only override (was CS-S1 self-override)
Purpose & workflow: When a safety screening (contrast, MRI, pregnancy) blocks a study, the technologist or desk can only request an override — they can never grant one. The request lands in a physician queue; the physician reviews the underlying screening data, must confirm their identity, give a clinical reason, and acknowledge the risk statement. A grant is time-boxed and stamped onto the study as a banner; every step is fully audited.

TK-04 Study hold / cancel — terminal states

MVP1-CORE
G6 Radiology Technician — workspace 'RIS · Technician'
Baseline: EXTENDS · RT-S2 hold/cancel → visible terminal states
Purpose & workflow: Technologists and supervisors use this screen to place studies on hold (with mandatory reason and auto-review timer) or cancel them against a fixed taxonomy. It must guarantee the radiation-delivered guard: once exposure has occurred a study can never be "cancelled" — it becomes the distinct terminal state abandoned after exposure, with the dose record retained forever. Terminal rows stay visible (struck through), and downstream parties (referrer, billing, reading) are notified automatically.

MVP1-CORE

Baseline: NET-NEW · closes RT-S2 flag-retake dead-end
Purpose & workflow: The technologist raises a retake when acquired images are non-diagnostic (motion, artefact, positioning, equipment). MVP1-CORE
G6 Radiology Technician — workspace 'RIS · Technician'
Baseline: NET-NEW · contrast administration record (lot/batch)
Purpose & workflow: The technologist records every contrast administration at the point of injection: agent from the branch catalog, concentration/volume/route, LOT & BATCH with expiry (scan or type), who administered and who supervised, with timestamps. RD-04 Viewer degraded states

MVP1-CORE
G7 Radiologist — workspace 'RIS · Reading'
Baseline: EXTENDS · RR-S2 degraded/edge states
Purpose & workflow: Defines exactly how the viewer behaves when things go wrong mid-read: image-load timeouts (retry, then archive re-query), low-bandwidth progressive rendering, lossy-compression guards ("not for final read below quality Q90"), crash recovery that restores the session with annotations intact, and a concurrent-open warning when two readers hold the same study. It must guarantee that no final report is ever signed against lossy or incomplete pixels, and that degraded conditions are visible, actionable and logged — never silent.

G7 Radiologist — workspace 'RIS · Reading'

Working offline is supported — actions queue and sync when reconnected. Signing is the exception: a signature only exists once the server confirms it. It is never queued silently.

Re-sends the identical signed payload (declaration tick 12:33:02, passkey assertion 12:33:11, content hash sha256:9c4e…b21a). If the server already recorded it, you get "already signed" — never a duplicate report or double release.

RD-10 Critical result — flag, tier & send

MVP1-CORE
G7 Radiologist — workspace 'RIS · Reading'
Baseline: EXTENDS · RR-S4 critical toggle → full flag/tier/send (NS-01, S-1)
Purpose & workflow: Used by the signing radiologist at the moment of report sign (or addendum sign) when a finding meets critical-communication criteria. It must guarantee a tiered acknowledgement clock starts (RED = 15 min, ORANGE = 4 h), that the outbound summary is SMS-safe with minimum PHI, and that a recipient is always resolved — verified referrer phone first, duty doctor fallback, or patient-directed script for self-referred patients. Send-now creates a tracked queue item in RD-11; the loop is only closed by a recorded acknowledgement.

What happens in Retract & rebind (Admin › Report governance)
Step 1
You raise a retraction request with the affected accession(s) and a mandatory narrative.
Step 2
Four-eyes approval: a second approver (branch admin K. Verma or branch medical lead Dr. A. Rao) must independently confirm — the requester can never self-approve.
Step 3
The report is retracted on both patient records with a visible retraction notice; every prior recipient is notified the report is withdrawn.
Step 4
The study is rebound to the correct patient/accession and returns to your reading worklist for a fresh report.
Change reasonOpen retract & rebind request

Break-glass emergency access
For genuine clinical emergencies only. Every break-glass event is logged in full and reviewed by the branch privacy lead within 2 working days.
⚠ Use only when a patient's immediate care depends on it. Break-glass bypasses normal care-team access controls. Misuse is treated as a privacy incident under Magnus policy and the DPDP Act 2023 and may lead to suspension of Doctor Desk access.
Before you break the glass Checklist
✓I have a genuine, time-critical clinical reason.
✓The patient is not already on my care-team list (checked "My patients").
✓A standard access request (4h SLA) would be too slow for this situation.
✓I understand all my actions will be tagged and reviewed.
🔒 If this is not time-critical, use Access requests instead — the branch privacy lead approves most requests within 4 hours.

BL-06 Refunds

MVP1-CORE
G9 Billing & Payments — workspace 'Billing'
Baseline: EXTENDS · BL-S5 refunds + failure state
Purpose & workflow: Cashier raises a refund against a paid invoice/receipt — amount can never exceed the collected balance and a reason from the taxonomy is mandatory. Refunds route through the async approvals queue (BL-08); once approved they process on the original payment mode by preference, with a justified cash fallback. Failed bank/UPI refunds bounce into a recovery state with retry or alternate-method options, and every refund lands in the immutable refund register.

G9 Billing & Payments — workspace 'Billing'
Baseline: EXTENDS · BL-S2/S5 approvals → NS-06 async queue

BL-09 Cash session & end-of-day close

MVP1-CORE
G9 Billing & Payments — workspace 'Billing'
Baseline: NET-NEW · NS-08 cash session & EOD close
Purpose & workflow: Each cashier opens a cash session with a counted float and closes it end-of-day through a fixed stepper: count → reconcile → resolve → sign. System totals by mode are compared against counted cash and gateway-settled digital amounts; any non-zero variance demands a reason and a supervisor countersign. The close produces an immutable CSH-NPV-2026-xxxx record, and gateway mismatches link straight into the BL-04 reconciliation ledger.

Place of supply rule explainer
CGST/SGST vs IGST — how Magnus decidesIf the recipient's place of supply is Kerala (state code 27, same as our GSTIN), a taxable line splits into CGST + SGST. If the recipient is registered in another state (e.g. a corporate payer with a Karnataka GSTIN), IGST applies. For walk-in patients, place of supply is the branch location — always Kerala, hence CGST/SGST.

BL-20 Report release policy & release queue

MVP1-CORE
G9 Billing & Payments — workspace 'Billing'
Baseline: NEW · expert-panel decision "Option C" — configurable release policy
Purpose & workflow: Implements the expert-panel decision Option C — organisation-configurable report release policy with authorised clinical override and full audit. The screen separates two statuses that the legacy system conflated: SIGNED (the clinical act is complete and the report is immutable — RD-09) and RELEASED (delivery of the report to patient/referrer is permitted — feeds NT-01 delivery). Policy is set once at organisation level (admin view, top); day-to-day the billing/front-office desk works the release queue (second frame). Reports flagged critical (RD-10) are never held for payment.

Billing › Setup › Report release policy
Report release policy ORG-LEVEL SETTING
Governs when a SIGNED report (RD-09) becomes RELEASED for delivery (NT-01). Effective-dated and recorded; applies to all branches of Magnus Diagnostics.
Release policy effective 01 Jul 2026
A — Release immediately on sign-off (payment independent)
Report is released to patient/referrer the moment the radiologist signs. Dues are pursued separately by the billing desk.
B — Withhold until full payment
Report stays SIGNED-not-released until balance = ₹0. No override path — not recommended; blocks clinically urgent delivery.
C — Withhold until payment, allow authorised clinical override SELECTED · PILOT DEFAULT
B behaviour day-to-day, but holders of release_without_payment may release on clinical grounds with reason + step-up confirm + audit. This is the panel-agreed pilot configuration ("B behaviour via C").
Change controlPolicy is org-level, recorded and effective-dated. Changing it requires Privacy Officer (S. Mehta) + org admin (K. Verma) joint approval; the change, both approvers and the effective date are written to the audit log. Last change: 01 Jul 2026 · B → C · CHG-POL-2026-031.

NT-07 Quiet hours & rate rules

MVP1-CORE
G10 Notifications & Delivery — workspace 'Notifications'
Baseline: NET-NEW · quiet hours & TRAI rules
Purpose & workflow: Central policy screen for when and how often Magnus may message patients. Per-channel throttles and a per-patient daily cap protect patients and sender reputation, with a full audit of every exemption used.

⚠ CLINICAL ALERTS ARE EXEMPT — NEVER QUEUED. Critical-result notifications to referrers and STAT workflow alerts bypass quiet hours, throttles and daily caps at all times. This exemption cannot be disabled. Every exempt send is individually audited (see State C).
TRAI classification note. All Magnus patient messages are transactional/service communications (appointment, preparation, report-ready, billing) tied to a service the patient requested — none are promotional. Magnus sends no marketing from Magnus; DLT templates are registered in the service/transactional category. Quiet hours below are Magnus's own patient-courtesy policy, stricter than the regulatory minimum for transactional messages.

What anonymity means here — please readWe will not record your name, phone, IP address or device details, and staff cannot see who filed this. But it also limits us: we cannot contact you for clarification or updates, we cannot fix anything tied to your specific bill or report without knowing who you are, and severity may be capped if we cannot verify safety details. You can still check status with your GRV reference and passcode.
Service — staff behaviour ▾
Privacy and clinical categories remain available anonymously; a clinical concern still pages the clinical lead even without a patient identity.
On 23 July around 6 pm at the North Paravoor centre, the front-desk queue for report collection had no token system and elderly patients were made to stand for over 40 minutes.
Avoid naming other patients or including anyone's phone/ID numbers — this text is visible to the handling team.

MVP1-CORE

AD-04 Roles & permission sets

MVP1-CORE
G12 Admin — Org, People & Master Data — workspace 'Admin'
Baseline: EXTENDS · AD-S3 roles & permissions
Purpose & workflow: Admins review built-in and custom roles through a capability-group permission matrix (read / write / approve / export) with ABAC condition chips such as own-branch-only, care-team-only and masked-by-default. Any change to a role is drafted, versioned and held pending approval by a second admin before it takes effect. A simulate-user preview shows exactly what a role sees before granting it.

MVP1-CORE
G12 Admin — workspace 'Admin'

Troubleshooting checklist (in order)
✓ 1. Confirm the modality console is powered on and out of service mode (contact MRI room ext. 4172).
✓ 2. Verify network drop: link light on wall port MRI-2-B; scanner shows IP 10.20.4.35.
3. From edge gateway, ping test to 10.20.4.35 — run via "Network probe" below.
4. If ping OK but connect fails: check scanner DICOM service restarted & listening on port 11112.
5. If AE title or port was changed on the scanner, request a registry update via Admin AD-08 (approval required) — do not work around with an unregistered AE (studies will quarantine, see IN-03).
6. Still failing after 30 min → raise incident, tag vendor AMC (Aria support, contract #AMC-2231).

Registry views, C-ECHO test runs (initiator, target AE, result) and AD-08 edit-link navigations are recorded in the access log. Device identity changes are only possible in Admin AD-08 under dual-control approval.

IN-03 Unknown AE & quarantine

MVP1-CORE
G13 Integration & Devices — workspace 'Integration'
Baseline: EXTENDS · RT-S4 unknown-AE → quarantine queue
Purpose & workflow: Studies pushed from AE titles not in the registry are quarantined instead of entering the archive — a privacy and integrity guard. Admins triage each quarantined study: register the sending AE (routes to Admin AD-08 with approval), associate it with a known device that was renamed, or reject with a reason. Study metadata stays masked until a decision is made; quarantined data auto-purges after 30 days.

Retention & privacy for quarantined data
Storage
Quarantine zone, encrypted at rest, outside clinical archive; not queryable via QIDO/WADO
Metadata masking
Patient name/DOB/accession masked in this UI; full values visible only after "Associate" or "Register AE" step-up confirmation
Auto-purge
30 days from receipt · warning banner at day 25 · purge is irreversible and logged
Rejection
Requires a reason code; sender is not auto-notified (network-level response only)

IN-06 Retry & replay console

MVP1-CORE
G13 Integration & Devices — workspace 'Integration'
Baseline: NET-NEW · retry/replay console (scope item #103)
Purpose & workflow: Failed HL7/DICOM/comms messages land in per-connector queues where staff can replay a single message or a filtered batch. Replays are idempotency-safe: every message carries a stable key, so a duplicate replay is acknowledged but suppressed downstream. Messages that fail repeatedly move to the POISON queue, which auto-raises an engineer task and suppresses further automatic retries.

GV-04 Deletion requests pipeline

MVP1-CORE
G14 Governance & Compliance — workspace 'Governance'
Baseline: EXTENDS · GV-S3 deletion pipeline + failure states
Purpose & workflow: DPDP erasure requests (DPDP-CR refs) move through received → identity-verified → assessed → approved → executed. Assessment splits data into delete-now, retention-held (radiology 10y, billing 8y, with keep-until dates) and legal-hold-blocked; execution is irreversible and therefore needs step-up identity plus a second approver. The patient is always sent a completion / partial-completion / refusal letter within the DPDP 30-day SLA; overdue requests escalate to the DPO.

GV-07 Legal holds register

MVP1-CORE
G14 Governance & Compliance — workspace 'Governance'
Baseline: NET-NEW · NS-11 legal holds
Purpose & workflow: Authoritative register of litigation/regulatory holds. Placing a hold requires a scoped selection, legal reference and step-up identity confirmation; releasing one is irreversible in effect and therefore four-eyes gated (Privacy Officer + DPO). While a hold is active it suspends retention deletion, blocks DSR erasure with a statutory citation to the requester, and forces counsel exports through a logged channel. Review cadence keeps stale holds from lingering.

Effects while a hold is active enforced by platform, not by convention
Retention suspended Held records are excluded from expiry batches (GV-06) at compile time; no destruction job can include them.
DSR erasure refused Erasure requests over held records are refused with citation — "retention required for compliance with law / legal proceedings (DPDP §8(7), §12(3))" — and the refusal letter is stored on the request.
Counsel exports logged Export-for-counsel runs only through the disclosure register: named recipient, matter ref, watermark, hash manifest, access-logged.

GV-08 Incident intake & triage

MVP1-CORE
G14 Governance & Compliance — workspace 'Governance'
Baseline: EXTENDS · GV-S4 → NS-15 incident front door
Purpose & workflow: Any staff member can report a security or privacy incident in under two minutes; the form nudges reporters to avoid pasting patient identifiers. Auto-classification flags "personal data likely" reports onto the breach path — statutory clocks start only at confirmation, not at report — and rules like "PII in logs" force-route to BREACH review rather than a low-severity ops bucket. Triage owners work a severity-and-SLA queue, with false-positive closure always requiring a reason.

G14 Governance & Compliance — workspace 'Governance'
Baseline: NET-NEW · consent registry & analytics
Purpose & workflow: Org-wide view of consent state by purpose (granted / declined / withdrawn with trend), notice-version adoption, and a per-patient lookup that stays masked until a documented reason is supplied. Withdrawals are traceable end-to-end: every suppression the withdrawal created (SMS, WhatsApp, teleradiology routing) is listed as an audit trail. Exports are aggregate-only by design.

Export policy

G14 Governance & Compliance — workspace 'Governance'
Baseline: NET-NEW · DPIA-lite register (Conditional)

IR-04 Corrections & resubmission

MVP1-CORE
G15 Imaging Regulatory — workspace 'Regulatory'
Baseline: NET-NEW · C-2 corrections/resubmission
Purpose & workflow: Once a month is acknowledged its Form F records are immutable, so any error is remedied through a correction record: it links the original FF, classifies the error against a reason taxonomy, and queues the correction for inclusion in the next monthly submission. The system generates a correction letter for the Appropriate Authority and maintains a register of corrections with authority responses. Creating a correction requires step-up identity confirmation plus a second approver (four-eyes: Dr. A. Rao, Privacy Officer).

PL-03 Suspend / close organisation — retention-safe

MVP1-CORE
G16 Platform Operator — operator console
Baseline: EXTENDS · PL-S2 + C-4 retention-safe close
Purpose & workflow: The platform operator can suspend a tenant (billing/operations pause, all data intact, tenant sees a banner) or run the retention-safe closure stepper: notice period → full tenant data export into patient-record escrow → read-only archive held for the statutory retention period (radiology records 10 years) → deletion only after retention expiry with DPO sign-off. There is no immediate hard-delete anywhere on this screen — every gate requires four-eyes approval and operator step-up identity confirmation.

PL-06 Support access

MVP1-CORE
G16 Platform Operator — operator console
Baseline: EXTENDS · PL-S5/S7 support access + revoke
Purpose & workflow: Operators never have standing access to tenant data. To assist with a ticket, an operator requests a tenant-approved support session with explicit scope and duration; the tenant admin approves, a banner appears in the tenant UI for the whole session, and every action is tagged. The tenant (or the operator) can revoke mid-session with immediate effect, and an evidence bundle of all actions is auto-shared to the tenant when the session ends.

Meter definitions Billing glossary
Study
One DICOM study registered and stored, counted at first C-STORE acceptance. Rejected/QC-discarded studies are excluded within 72h.
Storage GB
Peak stored volume during the month (hot + nearline PACS tiers), sampled daily at 02:00 IST.
SMS / WhatsApp
Provider-confirmed deliveries only (DLT Jio route, WhatsApp BSP). Failed/undelivered messages are not billed.
API call
Authenticated external API requests (HL7/FHIR + partner API). Internal service traffic is never metered.
Seat
Distinct staff account active in the billing month (≥1 sign-in). Patient OTP identities are never seats.
Tenant-visible mirror
Same numbers, both sidesEach tenant admin sees this exact meter under Settings › Subscription & usage in their own console. Mirrors update from the same metering pipeline within 15 minutes — operators cannot show a tenant different figures.
Mirror sync
IN SYNC last verified 06:00 IST
Discrepancies
0 open · 1 resolved in Jun (SMS retry double-count, credited)
Metering accuracyCounters are derived from immutable event streams and reconciled nightly against provider invoices (DLT SMS, WhatsApp BSP, storage layer). Reconciliation drift > 0.5% opens a metering incident automatically and freezes billing export for the affected tenant until resolved. Last reconciliation: 25 Jul 2026, 03:12 IST — drift 0.04%.

color.brand.primary#0F766E Teal primary. Primary buttons, active nav, focus ring, brand marks, KPI accents. Never used for status meaning — teal signals "interactive / brand", not "success". YES — tenant brand
color.brand.tint#CCFBF1 Selected rows, active-nav background, brand chips. Text on this tint must be #0F766E or darker. YES
color.sem.amber#F59E0B / text #92400E on #FEF3C7 Warning / at-risk. SLA nearing breach, overage, review-due, degraded provider. Amber always implies "act soon, not broken". Never decorate with amber. NO — semantic
color.sem.red#B91C1C / text on #FEE2E2 Danger / breach / destructive. OVERDUE SLA chips, critical findings, destructive buttons and modal top-bars, validation errors. Red is reserved — one red action per view maximum. NO
color.sem.green#15803D / text on #DCFCE7 Success / verified / within-plan. Completed steps, passing checks, delivered messages. Not for interactive elements. NO
color.sem.blue#0369A1 / text on #E0F2FE Informational / neutral status. Info banners, legal/court-order categories, in-progress non-urgent states. NO

Banners — five intents
InfoContext the user should know; no action required. Example: mirror-sync explanation on metering.
WarningAction needed soon; service still working. Example: SMS overage under soft-cap policy.
DangerBreach, destructive context or active privileged session. Persistent while the condition holds — never auto-dismisses.
SuccessCompleted operation with durable evidence (ids, timestamps). Prefer inline over toast for auditability.
RegulatoryCompliance/privacy framing: DPDP notices, retention rules, zero-standing-access attestations, metering accuracy.
Rules: one banner intent per condition; max two banners stacked before content; banner b line states the fact, body states the consequence and next step.

GhostTertiary navigation-like actions inside cards/tables.

DS-03 SLA & Escalation Pattern

DESIGN SYSTEM
G17 Design System & Patterns — documentation pages
Baseline: NET-NEW · NS-16 SLA/escalation pattern (product-wide)
Purpose & workflow: One countdown pattern for every timed obligation in Magnus — clinical (STAT reads, critical results), operational (unmatched studies, approvals) and regulatory (DPDP data-subject requests). Every SLA surface uses the same four visual states, the same owner chip, and the same escalation ladder so staff never re-learn urgency semantics between modules. This page is normative: product teams configure the schema in Section B; they do not invent new countdown treatments.
STATE A — THE FOUR COUNTDOWN STATES
Countdown chip anatomy — the only four allowed states normative
1 · On-track (< warn threshold)
⏱ 22m left · STAT read
Teal chip. Countdown in minutes. No owner shown — the assigned queue owns it. No pulsing, no sound.
chip.teal · "⏱ {remaining} left · {sla-name}"
2 · Warning (≥ warn %, default 75%)
⏱ 7m left · STAT read Owner: Dr. V. Shetty
Amber chip. Named owner chip becomes mandatory — an SLA in warning always has one accountable human, never just a queue.
chip.amber + chip.grey owner · row gains tr.hl
3 · Breached
OVERDUE +18m · STAT read Owner: Dr. V. Shetty
Escalated 14:42 IST → Radiology lead (K. Verma) notified via DLT SMS (Jio route) + in-app.Tier-2 fires automatically; quiet hours are never applied to clinical SLAs. Escalation line is permanent — it does not clear when the item is resolved.
Reassign nowAdd covering readerView escalation ladder
Word is always OVERDUE (uppercase) + elapsed overage. Actions render inline on the breached row — the user must never navigate to act.
4 · Resolved-late
Resolved · was OVERDUE +18m Closed by Dr. V. Shetty · 15:00 IST
Green chip, but the overage is retained in the label forever. Resolved-late items count against SLA attainment reports; the UI must not visually launder a late close into an on-time one.
chip.green · "Resolved · was OVERDUE +{overage}"
State usage rules do / don't
RuleDoDon't
One clock per obligationShow a single countdown chip per SLA per row, sourced from the server clock (IST).Never render two clocks for the same obligation, and never compute remaining time client-side from local device time.
Owner appears at warningAttach a named owner chip the moment warn % is crossed; auto-assign per config if unassigned.Don't show "Unassigned" on a warning/breached row — the escalation engine must assign before render.
Breach vocabularyExactly "OVERDUE +{elapsed}". Red chip.No euphemisms ("delayed", "at risk", "past due"), no blinking, no red row backgrounds — chip only.
Late closes stay visibleRetain "was OVERDUE +18m" in the resolved chip and in exports.Don't collapse resolved-late into a plain "Done" state anywhere, including dashboards.
SortingQueues default-sort: BREACHED (by overage desc) → warning (by remaining asc) → on-track.Don't let a saved user sort hide breached rows below the fold; breached rows pin above pagination.
prototype: alternate states below
STATE B — ESCALATION CONFIG SCHEMA
SLA definition schema — org-admin editable, versioned config contract
FieldType / defaultSemantics
sla.durationminutesFull window from trigger event to breach. Trigger event is defined per SLA (e.g. STAT read starts at study QC-complete, not at order time).
sla.warn_pctint · 75Percentage of window elapsed at which state 2 fires. Clinical SLAs may lower this (e.g. 50%) but may never raise it above 80.
sla.breach_owner_rolerole refRole that becomes accountable at breach if no individual owner exists (e.g. rad.lead, branch.manager). Resolved to a named on-duty person at fire time from the roster.
sla.tier2_delayminutes · 15Delay after breach before tier-2 escalation (next role up + SMS channel added). Tier-3 = tier-2 delay ×2, capped at org admin.
sla.channelslistIn-app always; tier-2 adds DLT SMS (Jio route); WhatsApp BSP allowed for non-clinical only. Patient-facing channels are never used for staff escalation.
sla.quiet_hoursenumnever-for-clinical Clinical class SLAs (STAT read, critical ack) hard-ignore quiet hours — this flag is read-only NONE for them in the admin UI. Operational SLAs may defer tier-2 SMS to 07:00 IST, but the in-app breach state still renders immediately.
sla.pause_ruleslistOnly allowed pause: patient-caused hold (e.g. patient left premises), recorded with reason + actor. No silent pauses; paused chips render grey "⏸ paused — {reason}".
Governance. Editing any clinical-class SLA definition requires step-up identity confirmation (TOTP/passkey) and a second approver (four-eyes) with the clinical.governance role. Config changes are versioned; live countdowns keep the definition version they started under.
Escalation ladder — reference rendering component: .ladder
Tier 0 · 14:00 IST — SLA started. Trigger: CT study MRD-2026-018834 QC-complete on CT-ROOM-1 (AE MERIDCT1), flagged STAT.
Tier 1 · 14:22 IST — warning (75%). Owner assigned: Dr. V. Shetty. In-app nudge only.
Tier 2 · 14:45 IST — breach +15m. Radiology lead K. Verma notified: in-app + DLT SMS (Jio route). Quiet hours ignored (clinical class).
Tier 3 · 15:15 IST — breach +45m (scheduled). Branch manager + org-admin dashboard flag; incident record auto-opened.

DS-04 Offline / Degraded / Sync Pattern

DESIGN SYSTEM
G17 Design System & Patterns — documentation pages
Baseline: NET-NEW · offline/degraded/sync pattern (checklist #13/#14)
Purpose & workflow: Indian diagnostics branches lose connectivity routinely; Magnus degrades predictably instead of failing randomly. This page defines the three-level banner hierarchy every module must use, the action-queue contract for offline-captured work, the sync-conflict resolution modal, and the hard capability matrix that says which modules may work offline at all. The matrix is normative — report signing is NEVER offline, no exceptions.
STATE A — BANNER HIERARCHY (THREE LEVELS, NO OTHERS)
Level 1 · Offline-supported (info blue) banner.info
⬇ Working offline — this module supports it. Front-office registration continues on the branch cache. 6 actions queued locally · original timestamps preserved · will sync automatically when the link returns. Last successful sync 11:42 IST.
RuleSpecification
When shownConnection lost AND the current module is marked full or partial in the capability matrix (State C). Pinned below the topbar, non-dismissible, updates queue count live.
ToneReassuring, factual. Always states: queue count, timestamp policy, last successful sync time (IST). Never says "error".
ForbiddenNo modal takeover, no toast spam, no per-keystroke warnings. One pinned banner is the entire treatment.
Level 2 · Degraded (amber) banner.warn
⚠ Degraded — some functions paused. PACS link to CT-ROOM-1 (AE MERIDCT1) is intermittent since 12:03 IST. Worklists show the read-cache as of 12:03 IST and are marked "cached". New study arrivals may be delayed; billing runs in draft-only mode. Owner: T. Okafor (technologist on duty) · auto-retry every 60s.
RuleSpecification
When shownPartial failure: one upstream (PACS, payment gateway UPI, DLT SMS, WhatsApp BSP) is down or flapping while the app itself is reachable.
Must state(1) which dependency, (2) since when (IST), (3) exactly what is paused vs. still working, (4) a named on-duty owner, (5) retry cadence. Cached data anywhere on screen carries a cached 12:03 IST chip.
ForbiddenNever show stale data without the cached chip; never let a degraded module silently drop writes — it queues (level 1 behaviour) or blocks (level 3), nothing in between.
Level 3 · Blocked (red) banner.danger
⛔ Report signing is unavailable offline. Signing requires a live server-side identity check and hash-chain write; it cannot be queued. Your draft for study MRD-2026-018834 is saved locally and intact. Signing re-enables automatically when the connection returns — nothing to redo. Why: a queued signature could be replayed against a report edited after you last saw it.
RuleSpecification
When shownUser attempts an action marked never-offline in the capability matrix. Rendered at the point of action (replaces the primary button area), plus the pinned level-1/2 banner stays.
Must state(1) what is blocked, (2) that in-progress work is preserved, (3) that recovery is automatic, (4) one-sentence rationale ("Why:") — users obey rules they understand.
ForbiddenThe blocked action's button renders Sign report disabled — never hidden, never enabled-then-erroring.
prototype: alternate states below
STATE B — ACTION QUEUE SPEC + SYNC-CONFLICT MODAL
Offline action-queue table — contract normative
#Queued (device, IST)ActorActionSubjectReplay orderStatus
112:04:11D. NairRegister walk-in patientA. Kulkarni (masked: A. K•••••ni)1 of 6Synced 12:31 IST
212:06:47D. NairBook USG appointment · US-UNIT-2A. K•••••ni2 of 6Synced 12:31 IST
312:09:02P. D'SouzaDraft invoice ₹2,850 (UPI pending)Enc MRD-2026-0188513 of 6⚑ Conflict — needs review
412:12:38T. OkaforMark patient arrivedEnc MRD-2026-0188524 of 6Held (after conflict)
Contract clauseSpecification
Queued timestamp preservedThe device capture time is the business timestamp forever — sync time is stored separately as synced_at. An SLA clock, a token number, an arrival time all use the capture time. The UI shows both when they differ by >5 min.
Replay orderStrict FIFO per branch per module. A conflicted item holds everything behind it that touches the same subject; unrelated subjects continue. Order is never user-reorderable.
Conflict flag⚑ amber chip, row highlighted. Conflicts never auto-resolve for clinical or financial fields; demographic no-ops (identical values) auto-merge silently and are logged.
VisibilityQueue is always inspectable (nav badge shows pending count). Nothing syncs invisibly except logged no-op merges.
Sync-conflict resolution modal — reference spec component: .modal

⚑ Sync conflict — Invoice draft, Enc MRD-2026-018851

Queued offline by P. D'Souza at 12:09 IST; the server record was changed by K. Verma at 12:14 IST while this branch was offline. Only the differing fields are shown.

FieldYour offline value (12:09)Server value (12:14)Keep
Discount applied10% (senior citizen)0% offline   server
Payable amount₹2,565₹2,850follows discount
Clinical-field rule (four-eyes). If any conflicting field is clinical (order, laterality, contrast flag, report content), single-user resolution is disabled: the resolver picks a value and a second qualified user (radiologist or supervisor) must confirm before the merge commits. Financial conflicts above ₹5,000 require cashier + branch manager.
Keep server valueKeep my offline value

Both versions, the choice, resolver and (where required) co-signer are stored in the conflict record — recorded in the access log.

Modal rules: shows only differing fields (never full-record diffs); derived fields render as "follows X", not as choices; "Merge both" is not offered — one side wins per field; dismissing the modal keeps the item flagged and held, it never discards either version.
prototype: alternate states below
STATE C — WHICH-MODULES-OFFLINE CAPABILITY MATRIX
Offline capability matrix (MVP-1) — normative, change requires clinical-governance sign-off exhaustive
ModuleOffline capabilityWhat worksWhat is blockedRationale
Front office (registration, appointments, arrivals)FULLRegister, book, reschedule, mark arrived — all queue with preserved timestamps.Cross-branch lookups (cached list only, marked cached).Patient flow must never stop for connectivity; identity dedup runs at sync.
Billing & paymentsDRAFT-ONLYDraft invoices, estimates, discount capture pending approval.Finalising invoices, UPI collection (payment gateway UPI requires live confirmation), refunds, receipt numbering.Fiscal document numbers and payment confirmations must be single-sourced server-side; duplicates are a statutory problem.
RIS worklistsREAD-CACHEView worklist/study status as of last sync, always chip-marked cached 12:03 IST.Status transitions, reassignment, priority changes.Two branches mutating one worklist offline creates unsafe double-work; reading stale is safe if labelled.
Report draftingFULL (local drafts)Dictate/type draft, templates, macros — saved to encrypted local store.Assigning drafts to other readers.Drafting is single-author; no shared state to corrupt.
Report signingNEVER—Sign, amend-and-resign, addendum sign.Signature = live step-up identity check + server hash-chain append at sign time. A queued signature could be replayed against content changed after the signer last saw it, and the signature timestamp would be unverifiable. No cached credential is ever acceptable. This row cannot be reconfigured per-tenant.
Critical results / STAT commsNEVER—Critical notify, ack recording.An unsent "sent" state is a patient-safety lie; the pattern requires live delivery receipts (DLT SMS / WhatsApp BSP).
Admin, config, user managementNEVER—All writes.Config drift across branches during a partition is unrecoverable by FIFO replay.
Legend: FULL queue-and-sync · DRAFT-ONLY / READ-CACHE partial with explicit limits · NEVER hard-blocked with level-3 banner. Any new module must declare its row here before build; "we'll decide offline behaviour later" fails design review.
Implementation noteFrontend: global ConnectionStatusProvider (React); offline actions queue in IndexedDB with client-generated correlation IDs and replay on reconnect. Backend edge service exposes IDEMPOTENT sync endpoints (correlation-ID dedupe). Offline registrations use temporary local UUIDs; the canonical MRN is assigned at sync; collisions route to the merge queue (FO-08).

Design-system pages are versioned artefacts (DS-04 v1.2, updated 21 Jul 2026 IST by K. Verma). Offline queue replays, conflict resolutions and capability-matrix changes are written to the immutable audit trail and recorded in the access log.

DS-05 Empty / Loading / Error Pattern

DESIGN SYSTEM
G17 Design System & Patterns — documentation pages
Baseline: NET-NEW · empty/loading/error pattern (review §5 gap)
Purpose & workflow: In a clinical product, "nothing here" and "we couldn't load it" are safety-different statements and must never look alike. This page defines the five canonical specimens — first-run empty, filtered empty, loading skeleton, error card, and service-down page — plus the copy tone rules every module must follow. The core invariant: Magnus never shows a partial list as if it were complete.
STATE A — THE FIVE SPECIMENS
1 · First-run empty has a CTA
🗓
No appointment slots defined yet
MRI-ROOM-2 has no schedule template. Create one to start accepting bookings for this room.
Create schedule template
or copy from CT-ROOM-1
RuleSpec
StructureIcon → one-line fact → one sentence of context → exactly one primary CTA (+ optional ghost alternative). Never two primary buttons.
Only when truly emptyShown only when the unfiltered dataset has zero rows AND the load succeeded. Verified-empty, never assumed-empty.
2 · Filtered empty clear filters, no CTA
🔍
No studies match these filters
142 studies exist today; your filters (Modality: MRI · Status: unreported · Reader: Dr. V. Shetty) match none.
Clear all filters Edit filters
RuleSpec
Must differ from #1Always states the total that exists ("142 studies exist") and names the active filters, so staff never mistake a filter for an empty worklist.
Primary action"Clear all filters" — never a create-CTA; creating data is not the fix for over-filtering.
3 · Loading skeleton no spinners > 400ms
RuleSpec
400ms rule<400ms: render nothing (no flash). ≥400ms: skeleton mirroring the real layout (same row count as page size, same column widths). Bare spinners are allowed only inside buttons for in-place actions.
No layout shiftSkeleton occupies the exact final geometry; counts/KPIs skeleton as blocks, never show 0 while loading — 0 is data.
TimeoutAt 15s the skeleton must resolve to specimen 4 (error card). Skeletons never persist indefinitely.
4 · Error card no partial lists rule
⛔ Couldn't load today's unreported worklist. What failed: the RIS query timed out at 09:14 IST (request req_7f3ka9).
What we did NOT show: a partial list. 37 of 142 studies had loaded — showing them could hide a STAT study in the missing 105, so we show none.
Your work is unaffected; nothing was changed.
Retry now View cached list (as of 09:02 IST)
RuleSpec
Three statements, always(1) What failed, in task language + request ID; (2) what we did NOT show and why — the no-partial-lists rule is stated to the user, not just enforced; (3) whether any user data/state changed.
No partial listsA list either renders complete-as-of-a-timestamp or not at all. Cached fallbacks are allowed but carry cached 09:02 IST.
RetryExplicit "Retry now" button + auto-retry with backoff; never silent infinite retry that masks an outage.
5 · Service-down page (full takeover) last resort
◎ Magnus
Magnus is temporarily unavailable
Since 09:41 IST · incident INC-2026-0719 · we are on it. Drafts and offline queues on this device are safe and will sync on recovery. For STAT reads during the outage, follow the branch downtime SOP (printed copy at the front desk). Status: status.magnus.numinacore.in
Auto-reconnecting · next attempt in 28s
Rules: used only when the app shell itself cannot load (otherwise use DS-04 banners); must name the incident ID, start time (IST), data-safety statement, the paper-SOP fallback for clinical continuity, and a public status URL. Never a blank page, never a raw HTTP error.
prototype: alternate states below
STATE B — COPY TONE RULES
Copy tone rules — apply to every specimen above normative
RuleDo — write like thisDon't — never like this
Facts before feelings"No studies match these filters." / "The RIS query timed out at 09:14 IST.""Oops!", "Uh oh!", "Something went wrong 😕" — no interjections, no emoji in body copy, no exclamation marks.
Blame the system, not the user"We couldn't load the worklist.""You have no permission" phrasing when it's actually a load failure; "Invalid input" without naming the field and the fix.
State data-safety explicitly"Nothing was changed." / "Your draft is saved locally and intact."Silence about whether the user's work survived — in clinical software, silence reads as loss.
Task language, IDs in mono"Couldn't send the SMS reminder (DLT route)" + req_7f3ka9 for support."Error 500: upstream connect error" as the headline; stack traces or vendor names as the primary message.
Time is always absolute IST"cached as of 09:02 IST", "since 09:41 IST"."a few minutes ago", "recently" — relative time on stale clinical data is unsafe.
One next stepExactly one primary action per specimen (Create / Clear filters / Retry).Three equal-weight buttons; "Contact your administrator" as the only option when a retry would work.
Empty ≠ error, everVerified-empty says what exists ("142 studies exist today"); errors say what failed.Rendering an empty state when the fetch failed — the single most dangerous copy bug in this product.
Privacy in specimensPatient identifiers in examples/errors stay masked: "A. K•••••ni · MRD-2026-018851".Full patient names or phone numbers echoed into error cards, logs, or support IDs.

Design-system pages are versioned artefacts (DS-05 v1.1, updated 21 Jul 2026 IST by K. Verma). Error-card render events carry the request ID into telemetry with patient identifiers masked, and cached-fallback views are recorded in the access log.

DS-06 Audit & Step-up Pattern

DESIGN SYSTEM
G17 Design System & Patterns — documentation pages
Baseline: NET-NEW · audit & step-up pattern
Purpose & workflow: Magnus is privacy-first under DPDP: every consequential screen tells the user, in one 🔒 footer line, exactly what is being recorded about their presence there — and every sensitive action re-proves identity before it executes. This page defines the audit footer phrasing per action class, the audit event schema, the step-up modal and its action matrix format, and the hash-chain / tamper-evident chips that make the trail verifiable.
STATE A — AUDIT FOOTER LINE SPECIMENS (🔒 PHRASING PER ACTION CLASS)
The footer line — one per screen, bottom of content, class .audit specimens
Action classExact footer specimenPhrasing rule
View (PHI read)Viewing this record (A. K•••••ni · MRD-2026-018851) is itself an access event — your identity, purpose "treatment", and the fields displayed are recorded in the access log.Present tense, "is itself an access event". Names the masked subject and the purpose basis. Users must know reads are logged, not only writes.
Create / editSaving writes a before/after snapshot with your identity and reason; the change is visible to the patient in their DPDP access report and recorded in the access log.Mentions before/after snapshot and patient visibility — edits to a person's data are disclosable to that person.
Sensitive reveal (unmask)Revealing the full mobile number requires a stated purpose and is individually logged with a 30-day review flag — recorded in the access log.Reveal events log per-field, not per-screen, and always carry a purpose picked from a closed list (never free-text only).
Destructive / irreversibleCancellation is irreversible and requires step-up confirmation and a second approver; the full request, both identities and the reason are chained into the tamper-evident audit record and recorded in the access log.Says "irreversible" plainly, names both controls (step-up + four-eyes) before the user commits.
Export / bulkThis export (214 rows, PHI masked per your role) is watermarked with your identity and expires in 72 h — generation and every download are recorded in the access log.States row count, masking level, watermark and expiry — exports are the highest-leak surface.
Operator (platform)Operator actions on tenant Magnus Diagnostics run under a support-access grant that expires 18:00 IST; the tenant's org admin sees this session in their operator-access report — recorded in the access log.Operator lines always disclose the grant, its expiry, and tenant-side visibility.
Rules: exactly one footer per screen; always ends "…recorded in the access log."; always begins with 🔒 (supplied by the .audit class); never legal boilerplate — each line is specific to what THIS screen records. A screen with no consequential access (e.g. this documentation page) may omit it.
prototype: alternate states below
STATE B — AUDIT EVENT SCHEMA + INTEGRITY CHIPS
Audit event schema — every event, no exceptions data contract
FieldExample valueRules
event_id / tsevt_01J9M2… · 2026-07-21T14:42:09+05:30Server-assigned, monotonic per branch; IST offset stored explicitly.
actorusr_kverma · K. Verma · role org-admin · staff realm (Keycloak) · session sess_88c1 · step-up: passkey@14:41Real identity + realm + session + the step-up method/time if one gated this event. Service actions carry the service principal AND the human who triggered them where one exists.
subject (masked)pat_5521 · "A. K•••••ni" · MRD-2026-018851Subject is stored as an opaque ID; the display name inside the audit UI itself stays masked — reading the audit log must not become a PHI side-channel. Unmasking within the log is itself a logged reveal event.
action / purposerecord.update · purpose: billing-correctionAction from the closed verb registry; purpose from the closed purpose list (treatment, billing, quality, legal, support), optional free-text amplification.
basisDPDP consent cns_2210 v3 / legitimate-use §7(b)The lawful basis pointer — consent record + version, or the statutory clause. No basis, no write: the API rejects basis-less PHI events.
before / after{discount_pct: 0 → 10}Field-level diff for writes; reads store the field set displayed. PHI values inside diffs are encrypted at rest separately from the event envelope.
co_signerusr_dnair · approval apr_0931Present when four-eyes applied; links to the approval record with its own step-up proof.
prev_hash / hash…9f3a → sha256:4bc1…Each event hashes its content + previous event's hash — the chain that makes the chips below meaningful.
Hash-chain chip list-level
⛓ Chain verified · 14,208 events · anchor #482 · 15:00 IST
Shown atop every audit log list. Green = recomputed hashes match through the latest daily anchor (anchor digests are written to write-once storage). Verifying is a read action, available to org admins without any operator involvement.
⛓ Verification running · 62% ⛓ CHAIN MISMATCH at evt 13,551 — incident opened
Amber while recomputing; red mismatch auto-opens an incident, freezes log exports, and pages the platform operator (R. Iyer). Red is never dismissible.
Tamper-evident record chip row-level
✓ Tamper-evident · sha256:4bc1…9e
On each audit event detail: this event's hash re-verified against its neighbours at render time. Copy rule: say "tamper-evident", never "tamper-proof" — we detect, we don't claim to prevent.
✗ Integrity check failed — do not rely on this record
A failed row renders with content struck through and its neighbours flagged; the record is still shown (evidence), never silently hidden.
prototype: alternate states below
STATE C — STEP-UP MODAL SPEC + ACTION MATRIX FORMAT
Step-up identity confirmation modal — reference spec component: .modal

Confirm it's you — signing report MRD-2026-018834

You are about to sign the CT Brain (plain) report for A. K•••••ni as Dr. V. Shetty. Signing is legally attributable to you and cannot be undone (amendments create a new versioned record).

Use passkey on this device
6-digit code
Backup codes work here; using one voids it and notifies you by SMS. Staff realm (Keycloak) · session sess_74d2.
CancelConfirm & sign

The step-up method, factor age and result are attached to the signing event and recorded in the access log.

Modal ruleSpecification
Names the exact actionTitle and body restate the specific action + masked subject ("signing report MRD-2026-018834"), never generic "Confirm your identity". What is confirmed is what executes — the payload is bound to the challenge.
Factor rulesPasskey preferred, TOTP fallback, backup codes accepted-and-voided. Password re-entry alone is never a valid step-up. Patient OTP realm factors can never satisfy a staff-realm step-up.
Freshness windowGrade A actions: fresh challenge every time. Grade B: a step-up ≤10 min old may be reused, shown as "verified 14:41 IST · reuse". Window is org-configurable 5–15 min, never longer.
Failure / cancel3 failed attempts locks step-up 5 min and notifies the user's other channel; cancel = no action, no partial state, logged as declined challenge.
Four-eyes compositionWhen dual-control applies, the second approver completes their own step-up on their own session — one person on two devices is blocked by same-user + same-device checks.
Step-up action matrix — required format (excerpt) every module ships one
ActionGradeStep-upReuse windowFour-eyesAudit class
Sign / amend reportAAlways, freshnone—Destructive-equivalent (legal attribution)
Reveal full patient contactAAlways, fresh + purposenone—Sensitive reveal
Refund > ₹5,000 / rate-card changeAAlways, freshnonerequiredDestructive
Merge patient records · delete study assignmentAAlways, freshnonerequiredDestructive
Bulk export (PHI)BYes≤10 min>1,000 rows: requiredExport
Edit demographics / discount ≤ ₹5,000BYes≤10 min—Create/edit
Routine worklist views, draftingCNo (session auth)——View
Operator: impersonate tenant user / tenant suspendAAlways, fresh (operator realm)nonerequired + tenant-visibleOperator
Format rules: every module's spec ships this exact six-column matrix covering all its actions; grades are only A (fresh step-up), B (reusable window), C (none). An action absent from the matrix defaults to grade A until classified — the safe default is friction.

Design-system pages are versioned artefacts (DS-06 v1.5, updated 21 Jul 2026 IST by K. Verma). Changes to footer specimens, the event schema, or any step-up grade require clinical-governance review with four-eyes approval and are recorded in the access log.

DS-07 Masked Identity & Privacy Pattern

DESIGN SYSTEM
G17 Design System & Patterns — documentation pages
Baseline: NET-NEW · masked identity & privacy pattern (C-7)
Purpose & workflow: Canonical rules for how patient identity is masked, tokenised and revealed across every Magnus surface. Every screen that renders a patient must consume the shared <MaskedIdentity> component — never hand-roll masking. Reveal is always an explicit, reasoned, audited act; masked is the default state everywhere.
Non-negotiable principleDemographics are rendered only when the viewer's role, purpose-of-use and context all pass the policy check. Failing any one of the three yields the token form — silently, with no error state that leaks existence of the record.

DS-08 Form Validation & Input Patterns

DESIGN SYSTEM
G17 Design System & Patterns — documentation pages
Baseline: NET-NEW · form validation & Indian formats
Purpose & workflow: Single source of truth for validation timing, error tone and India-specific input formats across all Magnus forms. Front-office registration (FO-*), billing (BL-*) and admin screens must import these field components — local format regexes are a review-blocking defect.
STATE A — VALIDATION TIMING & ERROR TONE RULES
Validation timing rules applies to every form, no exceptions
MomentRule
On keystrokeNEVER for names, addresses, free text. Permitted only for hard input filters (digits-only in phone/PIN) and live checksum hint on GSTIN/IFSC after full length reached.
On blurDEFAULT — validate the field the user just left. Error appears under the field, focus is not stolen back.
On submitFull-form pass; render an error summary card at top listing each failed field as a link that scrolls + focuses it. Submit button stays enabled — never silently disable.
Async checksDuplicate-patient, GSTIN registry, IFSC lookup run on blur with inline spinner ≤ 2 s; on timeout, allow save with UNVERIFIED chip rather than blocking front-desk flow.
Warnings vs errorsWarnings (amber) never block submit — e.g. “age 104, please confirm”. Errors (red) block. A warning acknowledged once is not re-shown on the same visit.
Error message tone say what happened & how to fix
Message
DON'T“Invalid input.” · “Phone number wrong.” · “Error 422.”
DO“Enter a 10-digit mobile number starting 6–9, e.g. 98200 12345.”
DO“GSTIN check digit doesn't match — re-check the last character (entered …Z4, expected …Z7).”
DO“Appointment date is in the past. Pick today (25 Jul 2026) or later.”

Tone rules: no blame (“you entered”), no jargon, no exclamation marks, ≤ 2 sentences, include a valid example where format is the issue. Errors are written in the UI locale (see DS-10); field values are never auto-“corrected” silently.

Required vs optionalMark required fields with * only. Never label fields “(optional)” — anything unstarred is optional. A form where > 70% of fields are required should be re-scoped, not decorated.

DS-10 i18n & Localisation Pattern

DESIGN SYSTEM
G17 Design System & Patterns — documentation pages
Baseline: NET-NEW · i18n & localisation pattern
Purpose & workflow: Rules for what Magnus translates, how Indic scripts render, and how locale interacts with legal notice versions. MVP-1 ships English (en-IN), Hindi (hi-IN) and Marathi (mr-IN). Staff UI locale is a per-user preference; patient-facing locale is a per-patient communication preference captured at registration.
STATE A — WHAT-IS-TRANSLATED MATRIX
Translation scope by surface locales: en + ml (Malayalam — pilot), hi/mr/ta ready
SurfaceTranslated?MethodRationale & rules
UI chrome (nav, buttons, labels, errors)YESManaged string catalogue100% key coverage gate in CI; a missing hi/mr key blocks release, falls back per chain (State C) at runtime only for hotfixes.
Patient comms (SMS, WhatsApp, portal)YESPer-locale approved templatesEach DLT SMS template is separately registered per language on the Jio route — translation is a new template ID, not a string swap. WhatsApp BSP templates likewise pre-approved per locale.
Consent forms & privacy noticesYESLegal-reviewed translations, versionedTranslations are legal texts, not string files. Each locale rendition carries its own reviewer sign-off and is bound to the notice version (State C). Patient signs the rendition they were shown.
Clinical reports (radiologist narrative)NOAuthored language only (English in MVP-1)Never auto-translated. Machine translation of clinical findings is a patient-safety risk (negation, laterality, hedging nuance) and creates an unowned legal document — no clinician has signed the translated text. Portal shows a hi/mr help note explaining how to get findings explained, but the report body stays as signed.
Master data (test names, modality names)PARTIALPatient-facing aliases onlyInternal catalogue stays English/coded (CT BRAIN PLAIN). Patient-facing alias per locale (“सीटी स्कैन — मस्तिष्क”) used on slips and portal only; invoices always print the English catalogue name + code beside any alias.
Audit logs, IDs, device namesNO—Log events, AE titles (MERIDCT1), document numbers are locale-invariant; only rendered timestamps localise.
Implementation notereact-i18next integrated from Sprint 1 even while only English strings ship — retrofitting i18n into components is the expensive path.

Line heightDevanagari needs headroom for matras and conjunct stacks: body line-height 1.7 (vs 1.45 Latin); buttons/chips min-height +2 px in hi/mr locales — components must not clip शिरोरेखा or descenders.
Font stack"Noto Sans Devanagari", "Mukta", sans-serif; embedded subset in PDF/A output (per DS-09). Never rely on OS fallback for print.
Type scaleDevanagari at same pt renders visually smaller — bump 1 px at sizes ≤ 13 px in hi/mr locale packs; never mix scripts mid-word.
TruncationNever ellipsis-truncate inside a conjunct cluster; truncate on word boundaries only. hi/mr strings run ~15–20% longer — layouts must pass the pseudo-locale expansion test in CI.
DigitsAlways international digits 0–9 (not ०–९) in all locales — clinical/billing safety rule; applies to slips, portal and SMS.
BidiNot applicable in MVP-1 (no RTL locale); layout stays LTR for hi/mr.
Number, currency & date locale rules
ItemRuleExample
Currency₹ with Indian grouping (3, then 2s) in all locales — grouping does not vary by language₹ 12,45,600.00
Date displayDD MMM YYYY; month name localises, order never does25 Jul 2026 · 25 जुलाई 2026
Time12-hour with am/pm for patients; 24-hour on clinical worklists; always IST label on printed docs02:15 pm · 14:15 IST
StorageLocale never touches storage: ISO 8601 UTC, paise integers, E.164 — render-time formatting only (per DS-08)2026-07-25T08:45Z
UnitsMetric only; radiation dose, contrast volume etc. never localised or converted120 kVp · 80 mL
Mixed-locale sessionsA hi-locale front-office user registering an mr-preference patient sees UI in hi while the printed slip and SMS go out in mr. Preview widgets must always render in the recipient's locale, with a chip: PREVIEW · मराठी (mr-IN).
prototype: alternate states below
STATE C — FALLBACK CHAIN & NOTICE-VERSION BINDING
Fallback chain runtime resolution order
1 · Exact locale
mr-IN string / template / notice rendition
2 · Language default
mr → hi is not assumed; each language falls back independently to…
3 · en-IN (platform base)
Always complete by CI gate; guaranteed terminal fallback for UI chrome and master-data aliases.
✕ No fallback for legal texts & DLT templates
A consent notice or registered SMS template with no rendition in the patient's preferred locale is not silently swapped to English — the flow surfaces an explicit choice: “Marathi version unavailable for notice v4 — proceed in English?” with staff attestation, logged.

Fallback events emit telemetry (i18n.fallback with key + locale) so the localisation backlog is data-driven; > 50 hits/week on one key raises an amber task for the org admin.

Translation version ⇄ notice version consent integrity
NoticeVersionenhimr
Privacy notice (patients)v4 · eff. 01 Jul 2026v4v4v3 pending review
Contrast consent (CT/MRI)v7 · eff. 12 May 2026v7v7v7
Teleradiology disclosurev2 · eff. 20 Jun 2026v2v1missing
Binding ruleA translation is valid only for the exact notice version it was reviewed against. Publishing notice v5 automatically demotes all v4 renditions to PENDING REVIEW — the consent flow then applies the no-fallback rule above until each locale is re-approved (legal reviewer + org admin, four-eyes).

Consent records store: notice version + locale rendition ID + rendition hash actually displayed — what the patient saw is provable byte-for-byte.

Locale preference changes, fallback attestations and notice-rendition approvals are recorded in the access log.

Matrix is enforced, not decorativeSidebar items a role cannot use are removed, not greyed. Rule: a cross-group hop must carry its context object (visit ID, order ID) in the route — the receiving screen renders pre-scoped, never asks the user to re-search what the previous screen already knew.

Deep-link & breadcrumb rules
RuleSpec
URL shape/w/<workspace>/<group>/<screen>/<entity-id>
e.g. /w/andheri-west/rd/worklist/V-260725-0412
No PHI in URLsEntity IDs only (visit, order, token) — never name, phone or MRN fragments; URLs land in browser history and proxy logs (DS-07).
Breadcrumb depthMax 3 levels: Workspace › Group › Screen. Entity context renders in the page title, not a 4th crumb. Crumbs are the route truth — no “fake” crumbs from arrival path.
Auth on deep linkUnauthenticated hit → AU-01 with realm inferred from workspace, then return to the exact link. Step-up-gated screens (PV-*, refunds) re-challenge even inside a live session.
Branch switchDeep link into another permitted branch prompts an explicit switch banner — never silently changes the active branch context.
Dead linksMerged/voided entities redirect to the survivor with an info banner (“Visit merged into V-260725-0398”), preserving the audit trail.

Denied deep-link attempts, branch context switches and cross-realm navigation events are recorded in the access log.
